plan.summary: An authoritative multiplayer game server in Rust for a simple top-down arena shooter, using WebSockets for broad client compatibility (including browsers), with fixed-tick server-side simulation, room/lobby support, and JSON-based messaging — sized as a solid demo/reference implementation rather than a production-scale system.

phases.name: Phase 1: Project Scaffolding
steps: Initialize a cargo workspace with two crates: `protocol` (shared message/state types) and `server` (the game server binary).
Add dependencies: tokio (full features), tokio-tungstenite, futures-util, serde, serde_json, uuid, tracing, tracing-subscriber, glam, dashmap.
Set up `tracing_subscriber` for structured console logging in `main.rs`.
Create a basic tokio TCP listener wrapped with `tokio_tungstenite::accept_async` to accept WebSocket connections on a configurable port (default 8080).
Verify a minimal echo server works end-to-end using a WebSocket test client (e.g. websocat or a small Node script).

phases.name: Phase 2: Protocol Design
steps: In the `protocol` crate, define a `ClientMessage` enum: Join{name}, Input{move_dir, action}, Leave.
Define a `ServerMessage` enum: Welcome{player_id, room_state}, StateUpdate{tick, entities}, PlayerJoined{...}, PlayerLeft{...}, Error{reason}.
Define shared types: `PlayerId`, `EntityState{id, position, velocity, health, facing}`, `RoomId`.
Derive Serialize/Deserialize on all message/state types via serde; document the wire format as JSON text frames over WebSocket.
Add unit tests in `protocol` verifying round-trip serialization/deserialization of every message variant.

phases.name: Phase 3: Connection & Session Management
steps: Implement a `PlayerSession` struct holding the WebSocket sink/stream halves, player id, and a channel (mpsc) for outbound messages.
On new connection, spawn a task that reads incoming WebSocket frames, deserializes into `ClientMessage`, and forwards them to a central room/game task via an mpsc channel.
Spawn a second task per connection that drains the player's outbound mpsc channel and writes serialized `ServerMessage` frames to the WebSocket sink.
Implement graceful disconnect handling: detect closed sockets or serialization errors, remove the player from their room, and broadcast a `PlayerLeft` message.
Add a heartbeat/ping mechanism (WebSocket ping frames every 5s, disconnect after 15s of no pong) to detect dead connections.

phases.name: Phase 4: Room & Lobby Management
steps: Implement a `RoomManager` holding a `DashMap<RoomId, RoomHandle>` where each `RoomHandle` wraps an mpsc sender to that room's dedicated tokio task.
On `Join` with no room specified, either place the player in an existing room with open capacity (e.g. max 8 players) or spawn a new room task.
Each room task owns its own authoritative game state (`HashMap<PlayerId, EntityState>`) and processes incoming `ClientMessage`s plus its own fixed-rate simulation tick.
Implement room lifecycle: rooms with zero players for >30s are torn down and removed from the `RoomManager`.
Broadcast `PlayerJoined`/`PlayerLeft`/`Welcome` messages to all players in a room via each player's outbound channel.

phases.name: Phase 5: Authoritative Game Simulation
steps: Implement a fixed-tick loop per room task using `tokio::time::interval` at 20 Hz (50ms per tick).

On each tick: apply the latest buffered input per player to update position/velocity (simple 2D movement with glam, clamped to arena bounds), resolve basic collisions (circle-vs-circle) between entities.
Implement a simple combat mechanic (e.g. melee/projectile hit detection based on facing + range) that updates health and triggers elimination when health <= 0.
After simulation, construct a `StateUpdate{tick, entities}` message snapshot and broadcast it to all connected players in the room.
Buffer only the latest input per player between ticks (discard stale inputs) to keep simulation deterministic and simple.

phases.name: Phase 6: Client Input Handling & Basic Anti-Cheat
steps: Validate incoming `Input` messages server-side: clamp movement vectors to max speed, reject malformed/out-of-range values, rate-limit inputs to at most 30/sec per player.
Ignore inputs from players not in `Alive` state or not yet fully joined.
Add basic sanity checks on join (name length limits, reject empty names, reject duplicate simultaneous joins from same connection).

phases.name: Phase 7: Testing & Tooling
steps: Write integration tests using `tokio-tungstenite` as a test client: connect, join a room, send inputs, assert state updates are received and reflect expected position changes.
Write a simple CLI test client binary (in a `tools/` crate) that connects, sends random movement inputs, and prints received state updates — useful for manual load/smoke testing.
Add a `justfile` or `Makefile` with common commands: `run-server`, `test`, `run-test-client`.
Document the JSON wire protocol (message shapes/examples) in `protocol/README.md` for future client implementers.

phases.name: Phase 8: Deployment Readiness
steps: Add configuration via environment variables (port, tick rate, max players per room, max rooms) parsed at startup with sensible defaults.
Add a `Dockerfile` using a multi-stage build (rust:slim builder + debian-slim runtime) exposing the WebSocket port.
Add graceful shutdown: on SIGINT/SIGTERM, broadcast a shutdown notice to all connected clients and close sockets cleanly before exiting.
Write a top-level `README.md` covering build/run instructions, architecture overview (per-room task model), and protocol summary.

manual_checklist: Decide on and open the desired network port/firewall rules on the deployment host.
If deploying publicly, set up TLS termination (e.g., via a reverse proxy like nginx or Caddy) since raw WebSockets here are unencrypted (ws://, not wss://).
Manually playtest with the provided CLI test client or a real browser WebSocket client to confirm feel/latency before adding more game features.

phases.name: Phase 1: Project Scaffolding
steps: Install kubebuilder, controller-gen, kustomize, and kind locally (documented in README, assumed present in CI/dev image).

Run 'kubebuilder create api --group apps --version v1alpha1 --kind AppService --resource --controller' to scaffold the CRD and controller.
Set up go.mod with module path and verify 'make build' and 'make manifests' work out of the box.
Initialize git repo, add .gitignore (bin/, config/crd/bases generated files noted, but keep generated code committed per kubebuilder convention).

phases.name: Phase 2: Define the AppService CRD
steps: Edit api/v1alpha1/appservice_types.go to define AppServiceSpec with fields: Image (string, required), Replicas (int32, default 1), Port (int32, default 8080), Env ([]corev1.EnvVar, optional), ConfigData (map[string]string, optional, becomes a ConfigMap), Resources (corev1.ResourceRequirements, optional).
Define AppServiceStatus with fields: Conditions ([]metav1.Condition), ReadyReplicas (int32), ObservedGeneration (int64).

Add kubebuilder marker comments for validation (e.g., +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0 on Replicas, +kubebuilder:validation:Required on Image) and +kubebuilder:subresource:status, +kubebuilder:printcolumn for Image/Replicas/Ready.

Write a sample CR in config/samples/apps_v1alpha1_appservice.yaml with example field values.

phases.name: Phase 3: Implement Reconciliation Logic
steps: In internal/controller/appservice_controller.go, implement Reconcile: fetch AppService, handle NotFound by returning nil.
Implement helper functions to construct desired Deployment, Service, and (if ConfigData set) ConfigMap objects from the AppService spec, setting OwnerReferences via ctrl.SetControllerReference.
Use controllerutil.CreateOrUpdate (or manual Get+Create/Update pattern) to reconcile each owned object: create if missing, update if spec drifted (compare relevant fields like image, replicas, env).
Watch owned Deployment/Service/ConfigMap via Owns() in SetupWithManager so changes to them trigger re-reconciliation.

Update AppService.Status after each reconcile: set ReadyReplicas from the Deployment status, set Conditions (e.g., 'Available', 'Progressing', 'Degraded') using meta.SetStatusCondition, and update ObservedGeneration.
Add requeue logic: requeue with a short delay if the Deployment is not yet ready.
Add finalizer handling if any external cleanup is needed (document as no-op finalizer example for extensibility).
Implement RBAC markers (+kubebuilder:rbac) for Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and AppServices (get/list/watch/create/update/patch/delete), then run 'make manifests' to regenerate role.yaml.

Implement ValidateCreate/ValidateUpdate/ValidateDelete to enforce Image is non-empty, Replicas >= 0, and Port in valid range (1-65535).

Implement a functional 'Add Habit' feature using a dedicated view, ensuring it saves the new `Habit` model to SwiftData.
Implement habit editing functionality (updating the habit name) directly from the list view or detail view.
Refactor the Habit List View to efficiently fetch and display at least the habit name and its current status (optional: e.g., 'Active' or 'Archived').

phases.name: Phase 3: Logging and Tracking Mechanism
steps: Develop the Habit Detail View, which shows a dedicated log for a single habit.
Implement the mechanism to record completion/non-completion for the current day. The logging function must check if a log entry already exists for the current date.
When logging, create or update a `CompletionLog` entry associated with the habit and today's date.
Implement logic to display a visually clear indication (e.g., checkmark/X) on the list/detail view based on the status of the latest `CompletionLog` entry for that habit.
Implement basic streak calculation: When querying the list, calculate and display the current consecutive streak length based on `CompletionLog` entries.

phases.name: Phase 4: Polish and Refinement
steps: Implement a comprehensive History/Calendar View showing logs for multiple weeks or months. This view should read and display all `CompletionLog` entries.
Refine the UI/UX across all views, ensuring adherence to modern iOS design guidelines (e.g., system fonts, appropriate spacing).
Add simple confirmations/alerts for user actions (e.g., 'Habit added successfully').
Incorporate error handling for data persistence operations and provide user feedback if data saving fails.

manual_checklist: Ensure the Xcode target is set to support modern iOS versions (iOS 17+ is recommended).
